Lady Liberty wasn't green. 🗽 Watch her go up: 10 years in 25 seconds. ⏱️

A granite pedestal rose inside an old star-shaped fort. She crossed the Atlantic in 214 crates, about 350 pieces. Gustave Eiffel's iron skeleton went up first, then a copper skin only 2.4 mm thick, hammered over wooden moulds in Paris and riveted on piece by piece.

The twist: she was unveiled in 1886 shining copper-brown. Salt air and rain turned her green, fully covered by about 1906.

Would you have kept her copper? Yes or no 👇

Next: Notre-Dame. Follow so you don't miss it.

yt_title: How the Statue of Liberty Was Built: 10 Years in 25 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
Hunt's granite pedestal inside Fort Wood on Bedloe's Island, 214 crates (~350 pieces) shipped from France on the Isère in 1885, Gustave Eiffel's iron pylon, and a copper skin about 2.4 mm thick hammered over wooden moulds (repoussé) and riveted on. Dedicated 28 Oct 1886 in reddish-brown copper; the green patina covered her by about 1906.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty · https://www.britannica.com/topic/Statue-of-Liberty
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
